title: The Interior Was Impermanent in the Past
html:
• Saṁyutta Nikāya 35.186 Linked Discourses 35.186
  • 17. Saṭṭhipeyyālavagga 17. Sixty Abbreviated Texts

Ajjhattātītāniccasutta The Interior Was Impermanent in the Past

“Cakkhu, bhikkhave, aniccaṁ atītaṁ …pe… jivhā aniccā atītā …pe… mano anicco atīto. “Mendicants, in the past the eye, ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind were impermanent.

Evaṁ passaṁ, bhikkhave, sutavā ariyasāvako cakkhusmimpi nibbindati …pe… jivhāyapi nibbindati …pe… manasmimpi nibbindati. Seeing this, a learned noble disciple grows disillusioned with the eye, ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind. Nibbindaṁ virajjati; virāgā vimuccati; vimuttasmiṁ vimuttamiti ñāṇaṁ hoti. Being disillusioned, desire fades away. When desire fades away they’re freed. When they’re freed, they know they’re freed.

‘Khīṇā jāti, vusitaṁ brahmacariyaṁ, kataṁ karaṇīyaṁ, nāparaṁ itthattāyā’ti pajānātī”ti. They understand: ‘Rebirth is ended, the spiritual journey has been completed, what had to be done has been done, there is nothing further for this place.’”
